question: The major focus of my recent travels has been visiting all of the UNESCO World Heritage sites. When I visit a new country, I feel like it helps me appreciate where I am staying for more than just a few popular sites I have seen on social media. I have been paying special attention to what they call "The List in Danger," and I like to prioritize those locations if possible. I have recently visited Cameroon and Chad, and I think that my next destination will be the Democratic Republic of the Congo in June 2025. While I am there, it is my dream to see a Kordofan giraffe. Where could I see them when I visit?

Because it is on the danger list, the park is a top priority for conservation‑focused tourism—exactly what you’re looking for. | | **When to go** | **June** falls within the core tourist season (January – August). • **African Parks** – directly via their “Visit Garamba” portal or via a specialized Africa safari operator. | | **Why this site fits your manifesto** | 1. **UNESCO World Heritage site** on the danger list (as of 2025).
2. **Only DRC location** for “Kordofan giraffes.”

• Funds in local currency (CFA F XAF) and some US dollars as an emergency buffer. | --- ### Quick “One‑liner”: If you go to **Garamba National Park** in June 2025, you’ll be in the only DRC location where Kordofan giraffes exist, visiting a UNESCO World Heritage Site that is still on the danger list and witnessing firsthand the survival of a critically endangered subspecies. A guided safari through the park’s northern “giraffe circuit” is the best way to see them. Good luck on your next UNESCO adventure!

tool_calls.result: The only place in the Democratic Republic of the Congo where you can see Kordofan giraffes today is **Garamba National Park**.* **Location** – Northeastern DRC, in Haut‑Uélé Province, roughly 100 km south of the town of Buta. The park covers about 4,900 km² of mixed savannah and dense forest.* **Designation** – UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 1980) and managed by African Parks in partnership with the Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature (ICCN).  * **Population** – The park hosts the last remaining Kordofan giraffe (*Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum*) population in the country. Reports from 2017 show fewer than 50 individuals; more recent monitoring (2025‑26) indicates the numbers have risen to just over 100, but the subspecies remains critically endangered.  * **Why it’s the best spot** – The park’s open savannah zones provide the only relatively accessible habitat for these giraffes, and the park’s conservation work (anti‑poaching, GPS‑tracking, patrols) has improved visibility for wildlife tourism.  Visitors usually see giraffes along the "giraffe circuit" game drives in the park’s northern sector, especially around the Nagero airstrip and along the Garamba River.* **Practical notes** – Garamba is not a large commercial tourist destination.  Access is limited to scheduled tours led by African Parks rangers; flights land at Nagero airstrip, and visitors generally need a guide.  * **Conservation context** – The Kordofan giraffe has a very low density in the park because of sparse acacia, frequent poaching, and predation.  Conservation efforts have been intensifying since 2016, with a growing population and more secure habitat.In short: to see Kordofan giraffes in the DRC, plan a guided safari to **Garamba National Park** in northeast Haut‑Uélé.
